title: अश्वत्थामा नाट्यकाव्यमा रस विधान
nepali: रस सम्प्रदाय पूर्वीय साहित्यशास्त्रीय सिद्धान्तको जेठो सम्प्रदाय मानिन्छ । रसविनाको काव्य प्राणविनाको मानव सरह हुने कुरा पूर्वीय सात्यिशास्त्रीहरूले उल्लेख गरेको पाइन्छ । ‘वाक्यं रसात्मकं काव्यम’ भन्ने मान्यता पूर्वीय साहित्यशास्त्रको मूल मान्यता रहको देखिन्छ । पूर्वीय साहित्यशास्त्रका यिनै सिद्धान्तबाट प्रभावित कवि माधव घिमिरेका काव्यहरूमा रसको उचित प्रयोग भएको पाइन्छ । नेपाली साहित्यमा उनलाई रसवादी कविको रूपमा चिनाइन्छ । उनका कविता काव्यका साथै नाट्यकाव्य लखे नमा पनि महत्त्वपूर्ण योगदान रहको छ । पूवीर्य साहित्यमा नाट्यकाव्य वा गीतिनाटक भन्ने छुट्टैै विधाको उल्लखे भएको पाइँदैन । पाश्चात्य साहित्यको मेलोडा«मा, अपेरा र ब्याले भनिने विधाको नजिक रहेको श्रव्यदृश्य विधाअन्तगर्त पर्ने गयात्मक, भावनात्मक, सङगीतात्मक र द्वन्दात्मक विधा नाटय् काव्य हो । यसमा कथानक, पात्र, संवाद, गीत (कविता), द्वन्द्व, अभिनय, परिवेश, उद्देश्य, भाषाशैली, संरचना, रसविधान आदि तत्त्वहरू रहेका हन्ु छन् । यिनै सिद्धान्तका आधारमा रही कवि घिमिरले वि.सं.२०५३ सालमा नेपाल राजकीय प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठान ( हालः नेपाल प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठान) बाट ‘अश्वत्थामा’ नाट्यकाव्य प्रकाशित गरके ा छन् । नाट्यकाव्यका तत्वहरूमध्ये अश्वत्थामा नाट्यकाव्यमा प्रयोग भएका रसहरूको चर्चा गरिएको छ । अश्वत्थामा नाटय् काव्यमा रसविधान शीषर्क को यस लेखमा रहेका सैद्धान्तिक पक्षहरू पूर्वीय सिद्धान्त र मान्यतामा आधारित पुस्तकहरूको अध्ययन गरी पूर्वीय साहित्यशास्त्रमा वर्णित शङगार, वीर, हास्य, करुण, रौद्र, भयानक, अदभुत, बीभत्स तथा शान्त रस गरी नौ वटा रसको सङक्षेपमा सद्धौन्तिक परिचय दिइएको छ । उक्त सिद्धान्तको मियोमा रही ‘अश्वत्थामा’ नाट्यकाव्यको सुरुदेखि अन्तसम्म पटक पटक अध्ययन गरी रस प्रयोगसम्बन्धी अध्ययन गरिएको छ । सो अध्ययन गर्दा शोध अध्ययन विधि र पुस्तकालय विधिको प्रयोग गरिएको छ । सिद्धान्त र अध्ययनबाट अश्वत्थामा नाट्यकाव्यमा रसविधानको के कस्तो छ अङगी रस तथा अङ्ग रसको निर्धारण गरी निष्कषर्मा पुग्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ ।
american_english: The rasa tradition is regarded as the oldest tradition of Eastern literary theory. It is found that Eastern literary scholars have mentioned that poetry without rasa is like a human being without life-breath. The view 'vākyaṁ rasātmakaṁ kāvyam' appears to have remained the fundamental principle of Eastern poetics. In the poems of the poet Madhav Ghimire, who was influenced by these very principles of Eastern poetics, a proper use of rasa is found. In Nepali literature he is recognised as a rasa-oriented poet. Along with his poems, his contribution to dramatic poetry is also important. In Eastern literature, no separate genre called dramatic poetry (natya-kavya) or lyric drama (giti-natak) is mentioned. In Western literature, the genre that belongs to the audio-visual category and lies close to the genres known as melodrama, opera and ballet — the narrative, emotional, musical and conflict-driven genre — is dramatic poetry. In it remain elements such as plot, character, dialogue, song (poem), conflict, acting, setting, purpose, language style, structure and the treatment of rasa. Based on these very principles, the poet Ghimire had the dramatic poem 'Ashwatthama' published in 2053 BS by the Nepal Rajkiya Pragya Pratishthan (now Nepal Pragya Pratishthan). Among the elements of dramatic poetry, the rasas used in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama have been discussed. The theoretical aspects of the treatment of rasa in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama presented in this article: after studying books based on Eastern theory and doctrine, a brief theoretical introduction to the nine rasas described in Eastern poetics — shringara, vira, hasya, karuna, raudra, bhayanaka, adbhuta, bibhatsa and shanta — has been given. In the light of the said theory, reading the dramatic poem 'Ashwatthama' again and again from beginning to end, a study related to the use of rasa has been done. While doing that study, the research study method and the library method were used. From theory and study, an attempt has been made to reach a conclusion by determining what kind of treatment of rasa there is in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama, and the angī rasa and the aṅga rasa.

In the poems of the poet Madhav Ghimire, who was influenced by these very tenets of Eastern poetics, a proper employment of rasa is found. In Nepali literature he is recognised as a rasa poet. As well as his poems, his contribution to dramatic poetry is of importance. In Eastern literature, no distinct genre called dramatic poetry (natya-kavya) or lyric drama (giti-natak) is referred to. In Western literature, the genre that falls within the audio-visual category and lies close to the genres known as melodrama, opera and ballet — the narrative, emotional, musical and conflict-driven genre — is dramatic poetry. In it are to be found elements such as plot, character, dialogue, song (poem), conflict, acting, setting, purpose, language style, structure and the treatment of rasa. On the basis of these very tenets, the poet Ghimire had the dramatic poem 'Ashwatthama' published in 2053 BS by the Nepal Rajkiya Pragya Pratishthan (now Nepal Pragya Pratishthan). Among the elements of dramatic poetry, the rasas employed in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama are discussed. The theoretical aspects of the treatment of rasa in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama set out in this article: after a study of books grounded in Eastern theory and doctrine, a brief theoretical account of the nine rasas described in Eastern poetics — shringara, vira, hasya, karuna, raudra, bhayanaka, adbhuta, bibhatsa and shanta — has been provided. In the light of the said theory, reading the dramatic poem 'Ashwatthama' repeatedly from beginning to end, a study relating to the use of rasa has been carried out. In carrying out that study, the research study method and the library method were employed. From theory and study, an attempt has been made to arrive at a conclusion by determining what kind of treatment of rasa there is in the dramatic poem Ashwatthama, and the angī rasa and the aṅga rasa.
